cells.detail: AER-1 does not claim RFC 8785: draft -26 Section 12 says it carries the producer's exact bytes 'rather than mandating a canonicalization scheme such as ... RFC8785'. Its own serialization (Sections 3.1 and 7.1: code point key order, ensure_ascii escapes) was run through the contract anyway as a measurement: 34 of 53 vectors match RFC 8785, 19 differ (non-ASCII escaped as \u, UTF-16 versus code point key order, lone surrogates accepted, 1e-06 style numbers). The serializer is written from the draft text, not the kit's code, so this is a measurement, not a failed claim.

cells.cell: single-receipt vectors (21 valid, 36 invalid, 1 profile-invalid) recomputed from draft -26 Section 6
cells.detail: Maintainer errata of 15 Nov 2026 (https://github.com/zambodotdev/aer-1/blob/9ef5c5a64f5e1d396bb8ce81c198854b99f8e5c6/ERRATA.md, E-2026-11-15-1): the maintainer confirmed this finding against the live corpus and calls the tension real and inside the draft. His reading: Table 1 governs the verifier duty, a 0.4 receipt without metadata_hash is evaluated on its other checks with the absence reported, and a consumer that needs tamper-evident metadata requires the member (Section 13). Draft -26 is closed and its text is unchanged, so the verdict stays contradicted against the text. Under his reading the ten vectors agree: 57 of 58 single receipts, and 145 of 146 checks across the kit (adapters/aer1-errata-reading-run.txt); the one left is lowercase-timestamp, below. 48 of 58 with draft-zambo-aer1-26 read verbatim (the latest revision; -27 is 404). Differs: 10 valid vectors (bound-04, deep-nesting, edge-numbers, empty-members, input-hash-multikey-20, large-payload, maximum-offset-timestamp, optional-members-18, typographic-unicode, uuid-v1-core). Each declares receipt_schema_version "0.4", carries no metadata_hash, and sits in the kit's valid/ set, where every file MUST conform. Draft reading: Table 1 makes metadata_hash 'REQUIRED when receipt_schema_version is "0.4" or later', and Section 6 step 4 says 'A "0.4" receipt without metadata_hash MUST fail.' So all ten are rejected. Kit reading, from its runner: 'Absence of metadata_hash is not failed'. So all ten are accepted, and the kit's own runner returns accept on these bytes. The draft's conformance bar (Implementation Status; Section 11 SHOULD) is byte-identical verdicts to the runners, so the draft's procedure and its conformance bar disagree on exactly these ten. Controls: adding a correct metadata_hash flips our verdict on 10 of 10 (the kit accepts the same digests); removing it from valid/real-04 flips ours to reject, while the kit still accepts it, even after created_at is moved one minute. With the kit's rule, 57 of 58 agree, and the remaining one is invalid/lowercase-timestamp.json: the kit rejects lower-case t and z, but RFC 3339 section 5.6 allows them and -26 adds no case rule. Under the verbatim reading that vector agrees on outcome only, because it also lacks metadata_hash.

cells.cell: chain commitments, Section 7.3 (8 vectors)
cells.detail: Maintainer errata of 15 Nov 2026 (https://github.com/zambodotdev/aer-1/blob/9ef5c5a64f5e1d396bb8ce81c198854b99f8e5c6/ERRATA.md, E-2026-11-15-2): the maintainer confirmed this finding against the live corpus. His reading: entry_count in a standalone commitment is never canonicalized, so it MUST be encoded as a JSON integer, 5.0 is a mistyped member and the commitment check fails closed on it, and the corpus is normative on this member. Draft -26 is unchanged, so the verdict stays contradicted against the text. Under his reading 8 of 8 commitments agree (adapters/aer1-errata-reading-run.txt), while commit-valid-1 (entry_count 5) and the seq 1.0 vectors stay valid, as he states. 7 of 8 against draft-zambo-aer1-26 (the latest revision; -27 is 404). Differs: x-entry-count-float, whose entry_count is written 5.0 over a 5-entry chain. Kit reading: it expects invalid, and its runner says 'commitment entry_count is not an integer'. That is Python isinstance(int); the JavaScript runner regex-rewrites the file to mirror that check. Draft reading: Section 7.3 defines entry_count as 'a JSON number with an integer value', so 5.0 is valid. Section 7.1 uses the same phrase for seq and adds 'The representations 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; both are accepted'. No sentence in -26 restricts how entry_count is spelled. RFC 8259 section 6 allows a fraction part and has no separate integer type. The kit itself expects valid for v07-seq-float-valid (seq 1.0, 2.0). Controls: spelling 5.0 as 5 flips the kit's runner to valid, and the case agrees. Spelling commit-valid-1's 5 as 5.0 flips the kit's runner to invalid, while ours stays valid.

cells.detail: The quote stays correctly signed; its pcrDigest differs from the approved composite and equals the composite we compute with PCR 3 extended by the swapped-artefact string. Our verdict Contested equals theirs. The run B nonce is not logged by the project, so extraData of run B is checked only to differ from run A, not against a nonce.

cells.cell: V3 forged platform evidence: one bit changed in the signed attestation structure of run A
cells.detail: Each of the 145 bytes of TPMS_ATTEST flipped in turn: the signature is rejected 145 of 145 times. The project's own tpm2_checkquote 5.4, run in their image on the same flipped copy, also rejects it, and accepts the clean quote with the right qualifying data. The draft's Section 13 run (a Veraison instance, EC P-256 key, PCR 4) is a different experiment and is not what is read here.

cells.cell: V4 stale replay: the run A quote checked against a different expected nonce
cells.detail: Signature valid and pcrDigest matching, yet extraData does not equal H(AEP digest : fresh nonce), so appraisal fails closed, as the draft's V4 requires; the project's run C reports Expired for the same input. This is the nonce comparison Section 14.1 says the unmodified Veraison reference scheme did not perform: our appraiser performs it, so the cell makes no claim about that scheme.

cells.cell: V5 outcome substitution: platform evidence kept, outcome changed (reverse binding of the outcome digest into the quote)
cells.detail: Both the project's forged outcome text and a copy of aep.json with its outcome_digest replaced give a different record digest, so extraData no longer matches while the signature and PCR composite stay valid: rejected, the outcome contributes to the signed qualifying data. The project's own check reports rejected. This tests the binding of the outcome digest, not the truth of the reported outcome (the draft says the same in Section 12).

cells.cell: V6 authority substitution or replay (platform affirming, application policy returns Unauthorised)
cells.detail: tpm-demo has no application layer. The nearest running code, the aep-sandbox attack scripts, returns DENY aep_sig_invalid for a swapped mandate (rejected at the package signature, not as an Unauthorised policy result next to an affirming platform appraisal) and ALLOW then DENY replayed for a reused one-shot nonce.
